main_body: Snow-covered log cabin: a large snow roof slope above a vertical plank wall with an arched double door and two small windows
top_band: Snow roof slope in white and pale blue with scalloped clumps, rows ~8-50, ending in a bright snow eave lip at rows ~47-50
evidence: Reading a column through the middle: the snow roof runs from about row 8 to 50 and is clearly a large sloped top surface, like the Beodeul tile roofs. A bright snow lip at rows 47-50 marks the front edge. Rows 52-54 are a dark shadow strip with icicles under the eave. The plank wall (rows 52-76) has its own shading. The door and windows read as inset: the door has dark frame edges and iron bands, and the windows have snow sills and dark surrounds. No receding side faces are drawn.

style.evidence: The snow roof uses about 5 steps from white through pale blue to slate blue, with per-clump scallops and shaded undersides, like the reference tile scallops. The wall has several browns with vertical plank grain, and the icicles, moss tufts, lit windows and door hardware add detail. Outlines are dark navy next to snow and dark brown next to wood, not uniform black. Tiles are information-rich and comparable to the reference.
